title: Hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over finite chain rings
abstract: We give a bounded-error quantum polynomial-time algorithm for finding hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ over any effectively presented finite chain ring $R$. We call auxiliary group elements or subgroups used to extract information through oracle queries \emph{probes}. For chain length at least two, elementary abelian socle probes first recover the complete flag modulo the maximal ideal. When the residue field has size $q\ge3$, we reconstruct the flag recursively, lifting rank-one terminal members one digit at a time. The intermediate digits reduce to abelian hidden subgroup problems, while the final digit is a finite-field multiple-shift problem solved using learning from subset and Fourier sampling. For $q=2$, where distinct flags can have the same stabilizer, we instead lift the conjugate parabolic subgroup through the congruence filtration. A final linear system determines it modulo normalizer directions. The algorithm outputs generators with probability at least $1-ε$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\log|R|,\log(1/ε))$. Consequences include $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})$ for every $N\ge2$ and, with an explicit maximal-order presentation, $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal{O_K}/N\mathcal{O_K})$ for number fields $K$.
summary: This paper presents a quantum polynomial-time algorithm to solve the Hidden Subgroup Problem for finding parabolic subgroups within $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over finite chain rings. It achieves this by iteratively using quantum probes to reconstruct the underlying algebraic structure, providing powerful tools for computational group theory.
main_problem: The paper develops a quantum algorithm to find hidden parabolic subgroups within the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ defined over a finite chain ring $R$. This is framed as solving a specialized Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP).
main_result: A bounded-error quantum polynomial-time algorithm is presented that can find the generators of the hidden parabolic subgroup with high probability. This has direct consequences for groups over $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ and number field quotients.
method: The algorithm uses quantum techniques, including oracle queries (probes) and Fourier sampling, to iteratively reconstruct the structure of the subgroup by recovering the associated reduced flag in stages.
model_or_system: The mathematical model is $\mathrm{GL}_n(R)$, where $R$ is an effectively presented finite commutative local ring (chain ring). The problem is purely algebraic/computational, leveraging quantum computational complexity theory.
key_observables: The generators of the hidden parabolic subgroup $H$, and the associated reduced flag $ ar{V} =  ar{U}_0 > \cdots >  ar{U}_m = 0$.
important_parameters: The dimension $n$, the size of the ring $|R|$, the error probability $\epsilon$, and the residue field size $q$.
main_assumptions: The algorithm assumes an effective presentation of the ring $R$ and that necessary algebraic structures (like transverse functionals) exist with high probability.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the general quantum algorithm for finding the reduced flag using socle probes (Chunk 2). It then details the recursive lifting procedure for the flag based on the residue field size $q$ (Chunk 1). Finally, it applies these techniques to specific, complex cases like number field quotients (Chunk 3) and general structural results (Chunk 4).
why_interesting: While the subject matter is abstract algebra, the core methodology is the development and analysis of quantum algorithms for solving structured computational problems (HSP), which is a central topic in quantum information theory.
